purpose: Site-wide compliance + AEO-concentration enforcement for Frame Restoration UT. Validator: scripts/audit-compliance-words.mjs. Legal basis: data/route-factory/UTAH-COMPLIANCE-LAW.md. Triggered pre-PR + CI on .html changes.

lineage.rule: Ported from TX v2 compliance gate 2026-05-30; dictionary re-authored for Utah law (TX §4102.163 / TDI do NOT apply in Utah).
lineage.adjustingBasis: Utah Code §31A-26-102(6) + §31A-26-201(1) — claim negotiation/settlement is a licensed act; an unlicensed roofer may not negotiate/settle/adjust claims.
lineage.deductibleBasis: Utah Code §13-50-302/-303 (Insured Homeowners Protection Act) — a residential contractor may not rebate/waive/pay an insurance deductible as an inducement; the homeowner is personally responsible for it.
lineage.licensingBasis: Utah Code Title 58 Ch. 55 (Construction Trades Licensing Act); DOPL classification S280 Roofing Contractor.

claimNegotiation.reason: In Utah, negotiating/settling a claim is licensed insurance adjusting (§31A-26-102(6), -201). A roofer may not advertise negotiating claims. Scoped to CLAIM negotiation only — ordinary 'price negotiation' / 'supplement negotiations' copy is allowed. Safe: 'document the damage', 'meet your adjuster on-site', 'provide a detailed scope'.

publicAdjuster.reason: Public adjusting is a reserved licensed role (§31A-26-102(9)). Frame is a roofing contractor, not an adjuster. Scoped to FIRST-PERSON claims of being/offering a public adjuster — educational mentions ('beware public adjusters who...') are allowed.

patterns: we'll cover it with a discount
cover your deductible with a discount
deductibleRebate.reason: Utah §13-50-302 bars a residential contractor from rebating/waiving/paying an insurance deductible (or implying $0 out-of-pocket) as an inducement; §13-50-303 requires stating the homeowner is responsible for it. Scoped to FIRST-PERSON OFFERS — 'you pay your deductible' (compliant), 'free roof inspection', and storm-chaser WARNINGS ('they offer to waive your deductible') are all allowed. 'Frame does not waive deductibles' disclaimers are fine.

patterns: handle all back-and-forth with your insurance
handle the back-and-forth with your insurance
work directly with your insurance company
work directly with my insurance company
coordinates directly with major utah carriers
claimHandling.reason: First-person claim handling / advocacy describes licensed insurance adjusting (§31A-26-201). Includes 'manage/handle/fight for/work directly with' the claim or insurer on the homeowner's behalf. Scoped to FIRST-PERSON — third-person ('your insurer will settle your claim') is allowed. Safe: 'we document your storm/hail damage', 'we meet your adjuster on-site', 'we supply a line-item estimate the adjuster can read'.

adjustYourClaim: walk the roof with your adjuster
deductibleRebate: the homeowner is responsible for the deductible
we handle the roofing work, you handle your deductible

insurance claim.reason: AEO concentration-over-repetition: concentrate jargon on the cornerstone (services/insurance-claims), distribute signal via FAQPage schema, not prose repetition.

deductible.reason: Deductible language is legitimate (the law requires stating homeowner responsibility) but should not saturate — concentrate on the cornerstone insurance-claims page + FAQ.
